-.summary: Broadcasts scalar subtraction from each element of the vector - Parameters: - lhs: The vector - rhs: The scalar value to subtract - Returns: A new vector with the scalar subtracted from each element

!=.signature: static func != (lhs: borrowing Self, rhs: borrowing Self) -> Bool

*.summary: Broadcasts scalar multiplication to each element of the vector (commutative) - Parameters: - lhs: The scalar value to multiply - rhs: The vector - Returns: A new vector with each element multiplied by the scalar

\/.summary: Broadcasts scalar division to each element of the vector - Parameters: - lhs: The vector - rhs: The scalar value to divide by - Returns: A new vector with each element divided by the scalar

+.summary: Broadcasts scalar addition to each element of the vector (commutative) - Parameters: - lhs: The scalar value to add - rhs: The vector - Returns: A new vector with the scalar added to each element

==.signature: static func == (lhs: TrueEffortScore, rhs: TrueEffortScore) -> Bool

accuracy.summary: Fraction of predictions that match the actual labels: (TP + TN) / total.

add.summary: Element-wise addition of two matrices - Parameter other: The second matrix - Returns: A new matrix where each element is the sum of corresponding elements

adjustedRSquared.summary: The adjusted coefficient of determination, `1 - (1 - R²) · (n - 1) / (n - p)` where `p` is the number of fitted coefficients (intercept counts when present in this convention).

AggregationMethod.summary: Specifies how values within a group or window are combined into a single result.

AggregationMethod.count.summary: Count the number of values in the group

AggregationMethod.max.summary: Select the maximum value in the group

AggregationMethod.mean.summary: Calculate the arithmetic mean of the group

AggregationMethod.min.summary: Select the minimum value in the group

AggregationMethod.percentage.summary: Sum all values per group, then normalize so all groups sum to 100

AggregationMethod.sum.summary: Sum all values in the group

agreement.summary: Whether the outlier-sensitive moment measure and the outlier-resistant Bowley measure agree, conflict by magnitude, or conflict in direction.

allSatisfy.signature: func allSatisfy(_ predicate: (Self.Element) throws -> Bool) rethrows -> Bool

analogy.signature: public func analogy(_ a: String, _ b: String, _ c: String, k: Int = 1) -> [(rank: Int, word: String, score: Double)]
analogy.summary: Returns the `k` words that best complete the analogy "a is to b as c is to ?". The classic example is `analogy("king", "man", "woman")`, which targets `king − man + woman` and typically returns `"queen"`. Returns `[]` if any of `a`, `b`, or `c` is not in the vocabulary.

anchorLabels.summary: The effort labels parallel to `anchorSamples`. The old-hard rows split between `.threshold` (sustained race pace) and `.hard` (climb, descent, and above-threshold surges) by their kinematics; that split is a judgment call, provisional until the validation study.

anchorSamples.summary: Classifier feature rows for the anchor set: [heartRate, pace, cadence, grade, vertOsc].

and.summary: Performs element-wise logical AND with another boolean array.

angle.summary: Returns the angle between two vectors in radians.

angleInDegrees.summary: Returns the angle between two vectors in degrees.

appendRow.signature: public mutating func appendRow(_ values: [String: Double])
appendRow.summary: Adds a row to the end of the dataset.

arange.signature: static func arange(_ start: Element, _ stop: Element, step: Element) -> [Element] where Element : Comparable
arange.summary: Creates a sequence of evenly spaced values within a half-open interval.

areValidVectorDimensions.summary: Returns whether all vectors in the collection have the same dimension count. Used to validate that a collection of vectors can be used together in mathematical operations.

argMax.summary: Returns the index of the largest element in the array.

argMin.summary: Returns the index of the smallest element in the array.

Array.summary: Fourier transform operations on real-valued signal arrays.

asArray.summary: The z-scores in the classifier's feature order: `[heartRate, pace, cadence, grade, verticalOscillation]`.

asChunks.summary: Turns a sequence of raw pieces into trimmed, numbered chunks.

asDictionary.summary: Returns the full word-to-vector dictionary. Useful when an algorithm expects a `[String: [Double]]` directly.

asExpression.summary: Returns the vector of fractions as a string, with each entry rendered by ``Fraction/asExpression()`` and right-aligned so numerators and denominators line up vertically.

asFraction.summary: Converts this value to its simplest fractional representation.

asFractions.summary: Converts each element to its simplest fractional representation.

asPercentages.summary: Converts each value to its percentage of the total sum.

averaged.summary: Calculates the element-wise average of a collection of vectors.

averageHeartRate.summary: The recorded heart rate averaged over active time, in beats per minute. Weighted by time alone, not by trust, so it matches the average a watch shows for the run. Present on every run, including a first run.

bandEnergy.summary: Returns the total energy contained in the frequency band defined by `range`.

baseline.summary: The baseline that scored this run, nil on a first run before any baseline exists. It is captured before `finalize()` refits, so it can differ from `tes.baseline`, which has already learned from this run. Read it with `baseline?.equation()`.

Bayes.summary: Bayes' theorem exposed as a stateless namespace.

BayesLikelihood.summary: The likelihood P(E | H_i) for each hypothesis under consideration.

BayesPosterior.summary: A labeled posterior distribution returned from multi-hypothesis Bayes.

BayesPrior.summary: A labeled prior distribution over a set of mutually exclusive hypotheses.

bestFit.signature: static func bestFit(data: [[Double]], k: Int, maxIterations: Int = 100, attempts: Int = 10) -> KMeans
bestFit.summary: Fits multiple K-Means models with different seeds and returns the best one.

bikeSharing.summary: 731 rows, 16 columns. Regression. Target column: `cnt` (total daily rides).

BinRule.summary: Names a rule for choosing the number of bins in a histogram.

BinRule.freedmanDiaconis.summary: `width = 2·IQR / n^(1/3)`, then `k = ⌈(max − min) / width⌉`. Freedman-Diaconis, 1981; robust to outliers.

BinRule.squareRoot.summary: `k = ⌈√n⌉`. Depends only on sample size. Quick first look.

bowley.summary: The Bowley quartile coefficient `(Q3 - 2·Q2 + Q1) / (Q3 - Q1)`. Bounded to `[-1, 1]`; resistant to outliers because it uses only the quartiles.

bowleySkewness.summary: Returns the Bowley quartile coefficient of skewness — a robust measure built only from the quartiles, so a few extreme values cannot distort it.

broadcast.signature: func broadcast(with value: Element, operation: (Element, Element) -> Element) -> [Element]
broadcast.summary: Broadcasts a custom operation with a scalar value to each element - Parameters: - value: The scalar value to use in the operation - operation: A closure that defines the operation to perform - Returns: A new array with the operation applied to each element

bundledURL.signature: private static func bundledURL(for csvFile: String) -> URL
bundledURL.summary: Resolves a bundled CSV path relative to the sandbox's working directory.

cadence.summary: Cadence, in standard deviations from the training mean.

callAsFunction.summary: Evaluates the polynomial at a single point using Horner's method.

catalog.summary: Returns a human-readable listing of every bundled accessor.

categoricalMappings.summary: Maps an original column name to the ordered class names produced when that column's strings were alphabetically encoded into `Double` indices.

cdf.signature: static func cdf(x: Double, df: Double) -> Double?
cdf.summary: Returns the cumulative probability `P(X² <= x)` under the chi-squared distribution with `df` degrees of freedom.

ceil.summary: Returns the ceiling of each element in the array.

centroid.summary: The centroid position for this cluster.

centroids.summary: The final centroid positions after convergence.

choose.summary: Returns a new array with elements conditionally chosen from this array or another.

chunk.summary: Splits a document into ordered fragments.

Chunk.summary: A single fragment of a larger document, paired with its position.

chunked.summary: Splits this document into fragments using the given strategy.

Chunker.summary: A strategy for splitting a document into retrievable fragments.

classDistribution.summary: Returns the number of samples per class as a dictionary.

classes.summary: The learned statistics for each class, one entry per unique label.

Classification.summary: A group of data points sharing the same predicted class label.

classificationReport.summary: Returns a formatted per-class classification report comparing these predictions against actual labels.

ClassificationReport.summary: A frozen snapshot of a multi-class classification's evaluation metrics.

classifier.summary: The effort classifier, seeded from the population anchors and any personal labeled samples. Frozen after seeding, since re-fitting it on its own predictions would be self-training.

Classifier.summary: A protocol for supervised classification models that predict discrete class labels.

classify.summary: Groups input features by their predicted class label.

ClassMetrics.summary: Per-class metrics for a single class label in a classification report.

classOrder.summary: Class labels in sorted ascending order — the canonical iteration order.

Cluster.summary: A single cluster from a K-Means model, containing a centroid and its assigned data points.

clusterCohesion.summary: Calculate average pairwise similarity as a measure of cluster cohesion.

clusters.summary: Groups the original training data into clusters with their centroids.

coefficients.summary: The fitted coefficient vector. When the model has an intercept the first element is the intercept; the remainder are feature weights.

Coefficients.summary: A model you can read the numbers out of.

column.summary: Extracts a column from a matrix at the specified index

columnLabels.summary: The label for each column, in column order.

columnNames.summary: Column names in their original declaration order. Reading `columns` directly returns a dictionary, which has no guaranteed order; `columnNames` is the canonical iteration order.

columns.summary: Per-column descriptive statistics, keyed by column name.

ColumnSummary.summary: A frozen snapshot of descriptive statistics for a single numerical column.

columnTotals.summary: Returns the total count for each column, in column order.

compactMap.signature: func compactMap<ElementOfResult>(_ transform: (Self.Element) throws -> ElementOfResult?) rethrows -> [ElementOfResult]

compare.signature: func compare<Comparator>(_ lhs: Comparator.Compared, _ rhs: Comparator.Compared) -> ComparisonResult where Comparator : SortComparator, Comparator == Self.Element

componentCount.summary: Number of principal components the model retains.

components.summary: The principal components, one per row — a (componentCount × featureCount) matrix. With three input features and two components requested, `components` has two rows of three values, and `components[0]` is the direction of largest variance. Each row is a unit vector, sign-fixed so its largest-magnitude element is positive.

conditionalByColumn.summary: Returns the conditional probability P(row | column).

conditionalByRow.summary: Returns the conditional probability P(column | row).

conditioning.summary: Conditioning of the standardized features — how redundant the signals are. A runner's pace, cadence, grade, and vertical oscillation move together, so this often reads in the tens, which is information rather than failure: the ridge penalty keeps the fit stable. nil when not meaningfully measurable. It is a 1-norm condition number of XᵀX, not an SVD condition number and not κ(X).

conditionNumber.summary: Returns the condition number of the matrix using the 1-norm.

ConfidenceInterval.summary: A confidence interval for a single regression coefficient.

confidenceIntervals.summary: One confidence interval per coefficient at the level specified when the summary was built (default 95%).

confidenceLevel.summary: The confidence level used to compute ``confidenceIntervals``, in `(0, 1)`. The default is `0.95`.

confusionMatrix.summary: Builds a confusion matrix comparing these predictions against actual labels.

ConfusionMatrix.summary: Captures the four outcomes of a binary classifier — true positives, false positives, true negatives, and false negatives — and derives standard evaluation metrics from them.

contains.signature: func contains(where predicate: (Self.Element) throws -> Bool) rethrows -> Bool

ContingencyTable.summary: A labeled two-dimensional table of integer counts.

converged.summary: Whether the off-diagonal norm reached the convergence tolerance within the sweep limit. An unconverged result is still a valid decomposition — the iterates remain exactly orthogonal-similar to the input — but its off-diagonal residual is larger than the tolerance guarantees.

correlation.summary: Returns the Pearson correlation coefficient between two vectors.

correlationMatrix.summary: Calculates the Pearson correlation matrix for multiple data series.

cos.summary: Returns the cosine of each element in the array.

cosineOfAngle.summary: Returns the cosine of the angle between two vectors.

cosineSimilarities.summary: Calculates cosine similarity between each vector in the array and a target vector.

count.summary: Number of training samples belonging to this class.

covarianceMatrix.summary: Computes the covariance matrix of a design matrix whose rows are samples and columns are features.

csvRow.summary: Returns the cells of the table in row-major order as a single CSV row.

csvRows.summary: Renders the summary as CSV with one row per column and one column per statistic.

cumulativeProduct.summary: Returns the running product at each position in the array.

cumulativeSum.summary: Returns the running total at each position in the array.

cumulativeTrapezoidal.summary: Returns the running area under the samples — total area accumulated at each time step, plotted as a curve the same length as the input.

currentEffort.summary: The classifier's effort band for the latest recorded sample, nil before the first sample.

currentResidual.summary: Observed minus expected heart rate for the latest sample, nil before a baseline exists.

currentScore.summary: The live True Effort Score, climbing through the run against the fixed 2700 anchor.

currentSignals.summary: The latest sample's signals as z-scores against the classifier's training distribution, so a UI can spot which signal is an outlier — a large negative `grade` with a near-zero `heartRate` is the downhill signature. nil before the first sample.

DatasetLoader.summary: Single chokepoint that converts a CSV file into a concrete dataset value.

decisionFunction.summary: Returns the raw linear score Xθ — the log-odds — for one or more samples.

degree.summary: The degree of the polynomial — the highest power with a non-zero coefficient.

degreesOfFreedom.summary: The residual degrees of freedom, `n - p`.

deltaTimes.summary: The per-moment durations, in seconds; the first is zero.

denominator.summary: The denominator of the fraction (always positive)

densities.summary: The power spectral density at each frequency bin, in units of `(signal²) / Hz`. Parallel to ``frequencies``.

derivative.summary: Computes the numerical derivative by dividing consecutive differences by the sample rate (time between measurements).

describe.summary: Returns a typed snapshot of per-column descriptive statistics.

description.summary: Human-readable summary of the dataset's origin, row count, columns, and any cleaning that was applied. For example, the bundled `iris` dataset's description records that it holds 150 rows across three species, four numeric features, and was originally published by R. A. Fisher in 1936.

determinant.summary: The determinant of the original matrix, recovered as the permutation sign times the product of the diagonal of `U`.

diag.summary: Creates a diagonal matrix from a vector of diagonal values.

Dictionary.signature: extension Dictionary where Key == String, Value == [Double]

diff.summary: Calculates the difference between each element and the element a fixed number of periods before it.

dimensions.summary: Number of components in each embedding vector — `50` for the bundled GloVe-50d slice.

discardRun.summary: Discards the in-progress run without folding it into history.

distance.signature: func distance(to other: [Double], metric: DistanceMetric) -> Double
distance.summary: Measures the distance between two `[Double]` vectors under the chosen metric.

DistanceMetric.summary: The distance metric used to compare two vectors.

distinct.summary: Returns the unique values in the array, sorted in ascending order.

distinctCounts.summary: Returns each unique value paired with the number of times it appears.

Distributions.summary: Probability distributions exposed as a stateless namespace.

divide.summary: Element-wise division of two matrices - Parameter other: The second matrix - Returns: A new matrix where each element is the quotient of corresponding elements

dominantFrequency.summary: The frequency in hertz of the strongest non-DC component.

dot.summary: Calculates the dot product of two vectors.

downsample.signature: func downsample(factor: Int, using method: AggregationMethod) -> [Element]
downsample.summary: Reduces the array size by grouping consecutive elements into fixed-size windows and aggregating each window into a single value.

drop.signature: func drop(while predicate: (Self.Element) throws -> Bool) rethrows -> DropWhileSequence<Self>

EffortClass.summary: The five effort categories. The middle three are named as training zones; the top category is named for the load itself, because it holds heavy muscular work as well as cardiovascular effort. The `threshold` category anchors the score, so one hour held at threshold reads 100 on the raw score, following the convention of power-based training stress scores.

EffortSignals.summary: The standardized signals for one moment — each value is the z-score of that signal against the classifier's training distribution, so a reading near 0 is typical and a large magnitude is an outlier. This is how a UI reads *why* a moment is unusual: on a steep downhill, `grade` is a large negative outlier while `heartRate` stays near 0, which is the calm-heart, hard-legs signature the raw numbers hide.

eigenDecomposed.summary: Computes the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of a symmetric matrix.

EigenDecomposition.summary: The result of a symmetric eigendecomposition.

eigenvectors.summary: Orthonormal eigenvectors, one per row. Row `k` pairs with `eigenvalues[k]`. Each eigenvector is sign-fixed so its largest-magnitude element is positive.

elbowMethod.signature: static func elbowMethod(data: [[Double]], kRange: ClosedRange<Int>, maxIterations: Int = 100, seed: UInt64? = nil) -> [(k: Int, inertia: Double)]
elbowMethod.summary: Computes inertia for a range of k values (elbow method).

elementsEqual.signature: func elementsEqual<OtherSequence>(_ other: OtherSequence, by areEquivalent: (Self.Element, OtherSequence.Element) throws -> Bool) rethrows -> Bool where OtherSequence : Sequence

embed.summary: Converts an array of words to their vector embeddings by looking up each word in the embeddings dictionary.

embedded.signature: func embedded(using embedder: some Embedder) -> [(text: String, vector: [Double])]
embedded.summary: Embeds every string in this array, pairing each vector with its source text.

EmbeddingIndex.signature: struct EmbeddingIndex<Label> where Label : Decodable, Label : Encodable, Label : Equatable
EmbeddingIndex.summary: An on-device vector store: embed each entry once at ingest, then rank the whole corpus against a query by cosine similarity.

EmbeddingIndex.Entry.summary: One stored entry: a payload and its embedding, in ingest order. `Codable` so a built index persists to disk and loads at the next launch.

EmbeddingIndex.Snapshot.summary: The persistable state of an index: its entries, labels and vectors, without the embedder.

EmbeddingsDataset.summary: A bundled word-embedding dataset — words mapped to fixed-length vectors.

empiricalRule.summary: Returns the observed and expected fractions of values within one, two, and three sample standard deviations of the mean — the 68-95-99.7 rule applied to your data.

EmpiricalRule.summary: Observed and expected fractions for the empirical (68-95-99.7) rule.

encode.summary: Encodes the pipeline, omitting the reducer key when no reducer is set so that reducer-free pipelines keep their original archive shape.

equation.summary: The fitted baseline as a readable equation with each signal named, such as `expected HR = 142.69 - 4.62·pace + 2.87·cadence + …`. It forwards to the wrapped Ridge's ``Coefficients/equation(variables:response:)``, so it reads the same way as every other linear model's equation. The weights are on standardized features, so each slope is the heart-rate change per standard deviation of its signal and the sizes compare directly.

exp.summary: Returns e raised to the power of each element in the array.

expected.summary: The expected values the wrapped model predicts for the given features.

expected1Sigma.summary: The fraction expected within one standard deviation for a Gaussian distribution (0.6827).

expected2Sigma.summary: The fraction expected within two standard deviations for a Gaussian distribution (0.9545).

expected3Sigma.summary: The fraction expected within three standard deviations for a Gaussian distribution (0.9973).

expectedHeartRate.summary: The heart rate the baseline expected for this run's workload, the session mean in beats per minute. Weighted like `meanResidual`, so the two add up to the trust-weighted average heart rate, which equals `averageHeartRate` when no reading was doubted. nil on a first run.

explainedVarianceRatios.summary: The fraction of total variance captured by each retained component. The values sum to 1.0 only when every component is retained (`componentCount == featureCount`); with fewer components the sum is the fraction of variance the projection keeps.

explainedVariances.summary: The variance captured by each retained component, largest first.

exponentialMean.summary: Computes the exponential moving average, where recent values carry more weight.

f1Score.summary: F1 score for this class — the harmonic mean of precision and recall. `nil` when either precision or recall is undefined.

falseNegatives.summary: Positive samples the model incorrectly identified as negative.

falsePositives.summary: Negative samples the model incorrectly identified as positive.

featureCount.summary: Number of features the model was trained on. Does not count the intercept term.

featureNames.summary: The regression feature names, in coefficient order after the intercept.

FeatureScaler.summary: A column-wise min-max scaler for feature matrices.

filter.signature: func filter<E>(_ isIncluded: (Self.Element) throws(E) -> Bool) throws(E) -> [Self.Element] where E : Error

filtered.summary: Returns a new panel containing only the rows where the mask is true.

finalize.summary: Closes the run: returns the breakdown, folds the run into history, and re-fits the baseline from the accumulated history (the classifier stays frozen). An indoor run returns its breakdown but leaves history and the baseline untouched. Returns nil when active `timerTime` is below the floor, in which case the run is cleared and not kept.

finalLoss.summary: The final penalized-loss value at the returned coefficients.

findDuplicates.signature: func findDuplicates(threshold: Double = 0.95) -> [(index1: Int, index2: Int, similarity: Double)]
findDuplicates.summary: Find pairs of vectors with similarity above the specified threshold.

first.signature: func first(where predicate: (Self.Element) throws -> Bool) rethrows -> Self.Element?

fit.signature: static func fit(features: [[Double]], labels: [Int], componentCount: Int, k: Int = 3, metric: DistanceMetric = .euclidean, weight: VoteWeight = .uniform) -> Pipeline<KNearestNeighbors>
fit.summary: Fits a scaler, projects the scaled features onto principal components, trains a K-Nearest Neighbors classifier on the projection, and bundles all three into a Pipeline.

flatMap.signature: func flatMap<SegmentOfResult>(_ transform: (Self.Element) throws -> SegmentOfResult) rethrows -> [SegmentOfResult.Element] where SegmentOfResult : Sequence

flattened.summary: Flattens a two-dimensional matrix into a one-dimensional array by concatenating rows in row-major order.

floor.summary: Returns the floor of each element in the array.

forEach.signature: func forEach(_ body: (Self.Element) throws -> Void) rethrows

formatted.signature: func formatted<S>(_ style: S) -> S.FormatOutput where Self == S.FormatInput, S : FormatStyle

fourierDominantFrequency.summary: Returns the frequency with the highest amplitude in the spectrum, excluding the DC component (0 Hz).

fourierFrequencies.summary: Maps each output bin to its corresponding frequency in Hz.

fourierFrequenciesHalf.summary: Returns only the positive-frequency half of the frequency axis.

fourierInverse.summary: Performs an inverse Fourier transform on real-valued input.

fourierMagnitude.summary: Returns the amplitude at each frequency bin.

fourierMagnitudeHalf.summary: Returns the amplitude spectrum for only the positive-frequency half.

fourierPhase.summary: Returns the phase angle (in radians) at each frequency bin.

fourierSpectrum.signature: func fourierSpectrum(sampleRate: Double, windowed: Bool = false) -> [(frequency: Double, magnitude: Double)]
fourierSpectrum.summary: Returns the positive-frequency spectrum as paired frequency and magnitude values, with automatic padding and optional windowing.

Fraction.summary: A rational number representation for educational display of numeric results.

frequencies.summary: The frequency in hertz for each density bin. Length is `paddedLength / 2 + 1`, where `paddedLength` is the next power of two at or above the input length. Values are evenly spaced from 0 to `sampleRate / 2` inclusive.

frequencyDistribution.summary: Returns a dictionary mapping each unique value to its relative frequency.

full.signature: static func full(_ count: Int, value: Element) -> [Element]
full.summary: Creates a 1D array filled with a specific value.

GaussianNaiveBayes.summary: A trained Gaussian Naive Bayes classifier.

GaussianNaiveBayes.ClassStats.summary: Statistics learned from the training data for a single class.

grade.summary: Grade, in standard deviations from the training mean. A large negative value is a steep downhill.

GradientDescent.summary: A regression model trained by batch gradient descent, and the shared optimizer behind every iterative model in Quiver.

GradientDescent.Outcome.summary: The outcome of the descent run that produced this model.

GradientDescent.Outcome.converged.summary: The convergence test fired within the iteration cap.

GradientDescent.Outcome.maxIterationsRea.summary: The optimizer used every available iteration without satisfying the convergence test. The returned coefficients are the best-so-far estimate, not corrupted — but a tighter learning rate or a larger iteration cap would reach the minimum.

GradientDescentError.summary: Errors thrown by ``GradientDescent`` when the optimizer cannot return a trustworthy result.

GradientDescentError.divergedIncreasing.signature: case divergedIncreasing(iteration: Int, previousLoss: Double, currentLoss: Double)
GradientDescentError.divergedIncreasing.summary: The loss strictly increased between two consecutive iterations by more than one tolerance unit. The descent step overshot the minimum without yet producing non-finite values. Recovering would require a smaller learning rate or scaled features.

GradientDescentError.divergedNonFinite.summary: The iterate produced a non-finite loss (`NaN` or `±∞`) at the given iteration. Typically caused by a learning rate that is too large for the feature scale — the parameters overshoot, the predictions blow up, and the squared residuals overflow.

grandTotal.summary: Returns the sum of every cell in the table.

groupBy.signature: func groupBy(_ categories: [String], using method: AggregationMethod) -> [String : Element]
groupBy.summary: Groups values by category labels and aggregates each group using the specified method.

groupedData.signature: func groupedData(by categories: [String], using method: AggregationMethod) -> [(category: String, value: Element)]
groupedData.summary: Groups values by category and returns chart-ready tuples sorted by category name.

hannWindowed.summary: Applies a Hann window to reduce spectral leakage before computing the Fourier transform.

hasIntercept.summary: Whether this model includes an intercept (bias) term. The intercept, when present, is never penalized.

head.summary: Returns the first rows of the panel as a formatted table.

heartRate.summary: Heart rate, in standard deviations from the training mean.

heartRateModel.summary: The Ridge model that predicts expected heart rate from workload.

heartRates.summary: The recorded heart rates, in order.

heatmapData.signature: func heatmapData(labels: [String]) -> [(x: String, y: String, value: Double)]
heatmapData.summary: Computes a correlation matrix and flattens it into labeled tuples for heatmap rendering.

histogram.signature: func histogram(bins: Int) -> [(midpoint: Element, count: Int)] where Element : BinaryFloatingPoint
histogram.summary: Divides data into evenly spaced bins and counts the frequency of values in each.

history.summary: The runner's accumulated workouts — the data the baseline is fit on, and the thing to persist. Grows as `finalize()` folds each run in; bounded by `historyWindow`, `minimumHistoryRuns`, and `historyLimit`.

historyLimit.summary: The most workouts retained, oldest dropping off first, applied after the window and the floor. It bounds the refit cost for a runner who logs many runs. nil keeps all.

historyWindow.summary: How far back, in seconds, from the newest run the baseline learns. Runs that start earlier drop off, so the baseline keeps pace with a runner who is improving. nil keeps every run.

hits.summary: The top-k matches, ranked best first.

hypotheses.summary: The hypothesis labels, in the same order as ``probabilities``.

identity.summary: Creates an identity matrix of size n × n.

imbalanceRatio.summary: Returns the ratio of the largest class to the smallest class.

index.summary: The position of this fragment in the sequence the chunker produced, starting at zero. A retrieved chunk reports this so the answer can cite which fragment it came from.

indoorGrade.summary: The grade, in percent, recorded for every sample of an indoor run. The watch cannot sense treadmill incline, so an indoor run is scored as level ground at the usual 0.5% setting; an incline the runner sets on the belt is not reflected.

inertia.summary: Sum of squared distances from each point to its assigned centroid.

info.summary: Returns a statistical summary of a 2D matrix including shape, size, type, and aggregate statistics computed across all elements.

init.signature: init(history: [Workout], labeledSamples: [[Double]] = [], labels: [EffortClass] = [], lambda: Double = 0.01, k: Int = 3, historyWindow: TimeInterval? = 28 * 86_400, minimumHistoryRuns: Int = 8, historyLimit: Int? = 60) throws
init.summary: Seeds from existing workouts and optional personal labeled samples, then fits the baseline once. Each labeled sample is a classifier feature row `[heartRate, pace, cadence, grade, verticalOscillation]`, appended to the bundled anchors, so the classifier never trains on less than the anchor set.

inverseTransform.summary: Maps projected data back into the original feature space.

inverted.summary: Returns the inverse of a square matrix.

iqr.summary: The interquartile range, defined as `q3 - q1`. Captures the spread of the middle 50% of the data.

iris.summary: 150 rows, 5 columns. Classification. Label column: `species` (encoded alphabetically as setosa→0, versicolor→1, virginica→2).

isAboveGate.signature: func isAboveGate(floor: Double, outlierZ: Double) -> Bool
isAboveGate.summary: Whether the top hit clears a relevance gate the caller defines: its score is high enough on its own (`floor`), or it stands out as a clear outlier above the field (`outlierZ` standard deviations).

isEmpty.summary: Whether the index holds no entries.

isEqual.summary: Checks if this array is equal to another array element-wise.

isGreaterThan.summary: Checks if each element in this array is greater than the specified value.

isGreaterThanOrEqual.summary: Checks if each element in this array is greater than or equal to the specified value.

isLessThan.summary: Checks if each element in this array is less than the specified value.

isLessThanOrEqual.summary: Checks if each element in this array is less than or equal to the specified value.

iterations.summary: Number of iterations the optimizer used before stopping. Equal to `lossHistory.count − 1` because the trajectory begins with the loss at the initial all-zeros parameters.

jacobian.signature: func jacobian(of f: ([Double]) -> [Double], at x: [Double], step h: Double = 6e-6) -> [[Double]]
jacobian.summary: The Jacobian of a vector-valued function, approximated by central differences.

name.summary: Short identifier — `"iris"`, `"titanic"`, etc., or for `Dataset.load(path:)`, the input filename without its extension.

next.summary: Returns the next random `UInt64` by scrambling the internal state.

ones.summary: Creates a 1D array filled with ones.

orthogonalComponent.summary: Returns the component of this vector that is perpendicular to another vector.

outcome.summary: Whether the run converged or hit the iteration cap. See ``Outcome``.

oversample.summary: Balances an imbalanced dataset by generating synthetic samples for smaller classes.

probability.summary: Returns the relative frequency of `value` in the array.

probabilityTable.summary: Returns a Markdown table of joint probabilities with marginals.

product.summary: Returns the product of all elements in the array.

record.signature: mutating func record(heartRate: Double, pace: Double, cadence: Double, grade: Double, verticalOscillation: Double, altitude: Double, at time: Date, hrTrust: Double = 1.0)
record.summary: Records one moment from its raw signals, stamped with an absolute time. The delta is derived internally, so the caller never tracks it. A non-positive delta is dropped, which self- discards a duplicate or out-of-order callback. The first sample of a run carries zero load but stamps the start; a post-resume gap advances wall clock only, never timer time or the run's start. `hrTrust` is the optical-sensor reliability, clamped to `0...1`; a fully doubted reading classifies on the kinematic signals alone. Grade is signed, negative for downhill; on an indoor run it is recorded as `indoorGrade` whatever the caller supplies.

SkewnessAgreement.agree.summary: Both measures land in their symmetric band, or both lean the same direction. The skew, whatever its size, is corroborated by a measure that ignores outliers.

TESError.summary: What the seeding initializer can surface, as one catchable type, so a watch app can handle a failed seed without trapping. The empty init and the live loop do not throw, and decoding a saved model restores its baseline as stored without refitting, so a `TESError` comes only from seeding with existing runs. `.baselineDiverged` nests the underlying `GradientDescentError` whole, preserving its typed payload and description.

TESError.insufficientLabeledSamples.summary: The seeding init was asked for more neighbors than it has labeled examples. The empty init preconditions `k <= anchorSamples.count` instead.

TESResult.summary: The breakdown of one finalized run. `adjusted` is the headline, but it never stands alone: `meanResidual` and the three session terms ride along as siblings, so a score driven by genuine hard work stays distinguishable from one driven by heat or altitude decoupling. There is deliberately no `score()` accessor that hides them.

topZScore.summary: How many standard deviations the top hit sits above the field's mean. Zero when the field has no spread (every score identical).

totalSupport.summary: Total number of samples across all classes.

trainingFeatures.summary: The training feature vectors, stored for distance computation at prediction time.

trainingLabels.summary: The training labels, one per feature vector.

trainTestSplit.signature: func trainTestSplit(testRatio: Double, seed: UInt64) -> (train: [Element], test: [Element])
trainTestSplit.summary: Splits the array into training and testing subsets using a seeded shuffle for reproducible results.

transform.summary: Transforms a feature matrix using the parameters learned at fit time.

transformedBy.summary: Transforms this vector using a matrix (matrix-vector multiplication).

Transformer.summary: A fitted preprocessing stage that maps a feature matrix to a new one.

transpose.summary: Returns the transpose of a matrix

transposed.summary: Returns the transpose of a matrix (convenience method matching Swift naming conventions)

trapezoidalIntegral.summary: Returns the area under the curve traced by the samples using the trapezoid rule.

trimmed.summary: Returns a polynomial with trailing zero coefficients removed.

TrueEffortScore.summary: `TrueEffortScore` models a runner's effort using three components: a `Ridge` baseline to predict heart rate from workload, a `ResidualModel` to measure the gap, and a `Pipeline<KNearestNeighbors>` to classify effort. It tracks session history, scores runs in real time, and updates the baseline as new data is collected.

trueIndices.summary: Returns the indices of all `true` elements in the boolean array.

trueNegatives.summary: Negative samples the model correctly identified as negative.

truePositives.summary: Positive samples the model correctly identified as positive.

tStatistics.summary: One t-statistic per coefficient. Equal to `coefficient / standardError`.

unique.summary: Returns the unique values in a column, sorted ascending.

updateRow.signature: public mutating func updateRow(at index: Int, with values: [String: Double])
updateRow.summary: Changes the named columns of one row and leaves the other columns as they were.

upper.summary: The upper bound of the interval.

value.summary: Reconstructs the determinant value (sign times exp of log absolute value)

valueCounts.signature: func valueCounts(column: String) -> [(value: Double, count: Int)]?
valueCounts.summary: Returns the frequency of each unique value in a column.

variance.summary: Returns the variance of a Poisson distribution. Equal to the rate `lambda`.

variances.summary: Variance of each feature for samples in this class.

vector.summary: The stored embedding for the first entry whose label equals `label`, or `nil` if no such entry exists.

VectorForm.summary: The visual form a vector takes when rendered via `asExpression()`.

VectorForm.column.summary: Column form with stacked Unicode brackets — the textbook default.

VectorForm.inline.summary: Inline angle-bracket form, `⟨a, b, c⟩` — the prose-friendly variant.

vectorProjection.summary: Calculates the vector projection of this vector onto another vector.

vectors.summary: The stored vectors, in ingest order — the corpus matrix. Pair any two to inspect their similarity directly, e.g. `index.vectors[i].cosineOfAngle(with: index.vectors[j])`.

version.summary: Library version. Keep in sync with the package tag at release time.

verticalOscillation.summary: Vertical oscillation, in standard deviations from the training mean.

vocabulary.summary: Every word in the dataset, sorted by rank ascending. `vocabulary[0]` is the most-frequent word (`"the"` in the bundled GloVe slice).

VoteWeight.summary: The weighting strategy for neighbor votes in K-Nearest Neighbors.

VoteWeight.distance.summary: Closer neighbors get more influence: weight = 1 / distance.

VoteWeight.uniform.summary: Each neighbor gets one vote regardless of distance.

weight.summary: The category's load weight. Public because the weights are published math — the raw score is `100 × Σ(weight·Δt) / 2700` — and a reader has to be able to reach them. Recovery is 0.1 because level walking costs roughly a third to a half of easy running per minute.

weightedAverage.summary: Mean of per-class metrics weighted by support.

withContiguousStorageIfAvailable.signature: func withContiguousStorageIfAvailable<R>(_ body: (UnsafeBufferPointer<Self.Element>) throws -> R) rethrows -> R?

within1Sigma.summary: The observed fraction of values within one standard deviation of the mean.

within2Sigma.summary: The observed fraction of values within two standard deviations of the mean.

within3Sigma.summary: The observed fraction of values within three standard deviations of the mean.

Workout.summary: A completed run, folded into history and the unit the baseline is fit on. Each moment is stored as raw signal values rather than a wrapper type, so a caller reads a workout back the same way they recorded it. Heart rate is stored as an outcome: the baseline's regression target and one of the classifier's inputs.

WorkoutLocation.summary: Where a run takes place. The watch cannot sense treadmill incline: its barometric altimeter measures a change in altitude, and a runner on an inclined belt never rises. An indoor run is therefore scored at a fixed level-ground grade and kept out of the personal baseline, so a grade the model cannot trust never shapes the runner's outdoor expectations.

zeros.summary: Creates a 1D array filled with zeros.

zScore.signature: func zScore(of value: Element, ddof: Int = 1) -> Element?
zScore.summary: Standardizes a single value against this array's mean and standard deviation, returning how many standard deviations the value sits from the mean: `(value - mean) / standardDeviation`.
